+# Hanna's OEIS A381355 prime-index divisibility
+
+## Abstract
+
+An integral source series exists and its logarithmic derivative satisfies Hanna's prime divisibility.
+
+The prime function is PrimePowerShiftLogDerivative.prime, the one-based prime schedule with prime(1)=2. The series have rational coefficients. Natural subtraction specifies the coefficient index n-1, and the asserted indices satisfy n>1. The inverse is formal power-series inversion. Casts to the rationals are displayed explicitly.
+
+**Definition 1.1 (The source equations).**
+
+$$\forall (F: \operatorname{PowerSeries}\left(\mathbb{Q}\right)), \operatorname{IsSourceSeries}\left(F\right) \iff (\operatorname{coeff}\left(0, F\right) = 1) \land ((\operatorname{coeff}\left(1, F\right) = 1) \land (\forall (n: \mathbb{N}), (1 < n) \implies (\operatorname{coeff}\left(n, F^{\operatorname{PrimePowerShiftLogDerivative}.\operatorname{prime}\left(n\right)}\right) = 0)))$$
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S1/Recurrence/Invariants/HannaPrimeIndexLogDivisibility.IsSourceSeries` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Citation.* Paul D. Hanna (2025). *OEIS A381355: prime-index divisibility of the logarithmic derivative of A381353*. URL: <https://oeis.org/A381355>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+OEIS A381353 NAME: "G.f. A(x) satisfies [x^n] A(x)^prime(n) = 0 for n > 1." Its PROGRAM initializes "my(A=[1,1])", fixing coefficients zero and one to one. These are the NAME and PROGRAM sections of revision 19; the entry has no page numbers. The source's A(x) is denoted F here, and coeff extracts a coefficient indexed from zero.
+
+**Definition 1.2 (The sequence and its index).**
+
+$$\forall (F: \operatorname{PowerSeries}\left(\mathbb{Q}\right)), \forall (n: \mathbb{N}), \operatorname{sourceTerm}\left(F, n\right) = \operatorname{coeff}\left(n - 1, (\operatorname{derivative}\left(F\right) \cdot (F)^{-1})\right)$$
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S1/Recurrence/Invariants/HannaPrimeIndexLogDivisibility.sourceTerm` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Citation.* Paul D. Hanna (2025). *OEIS A381355: prime-index divisibility of the logarithmic derivative of A381353*. URL: <https://oeis.org/A381355>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+OEIS A381355 NAME: "G.f. A(x) = x*F'(x)/F(x) where F(x) is the g.f. of A381353 that satisfies [x^n] F(x)^prime(n) = 0 for n > 1." This is the NAME section of revision 13, without page numbers. The entry's offset is one: its nth term is coeff (n-1) (derivative F * F⁻¹). The definition is total at zero, which is outside the asserted range.
+
+**Definition 1.3 (Hanna's conjecture with source existence).**
+
+$$claim = ((\exists (F: \operatorname{PowerSeries}\left(\mathbb{Q}\right)), \operatorname{IsSourceSeries}\left(F\right)) \land (\forall (F: \operatorname{PowerSeries}\left(\mathbb{Q}\right)), (\operatorname{IsSourceSeries}\left(F\right)) \implies (\forall (n: \mathbb{N}), (1 < n) \implies (\exists (z: \mathbb{Z}), \operatorname{sourceTerm}\left(F, n\right) = (\operatorname{PrimePowerShiftLogDerivative}.\operatorname{prime}\left(n\right): \mathbb{Q}) \cdot (z: \mathbb{Q})))))$$
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S1/Recurrence/Invariants/HannaPrimeIndexLogDivisibility.claim` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Citation.* Paul D. Hanna (2025). *OEIS A381355: prime-index divisibility of the logarithmic derivative of A381353*. URL: <https://oeis.org/A381355>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+OEIS A381355 COMMENTS: "Conjecture: a(n) is divisible by prime(n) for n > 1." This is the COMMENTS section of revision 13, without page numbers. The first conjunct asserts existence of a rational source series. The second ranges over every such series. An integer z witnesses divisibility inside the rationals.
+
+**Theorem 1.4 (Existence and prime divisibility).**
+
+$$(\exists (F: \operatorname{PowerSeries}\left(\mathbb{Q}\right)), \operatorname{IsSourceSeries}\left(F\right)) \land (\forall (F: \operatorname{PowerSeries}\left(\mathbb{Q}\right)), (\operatorname{IsSourceSeries}\left(F\right)) \implies (\forall (n: \mathbb{N}), (1 < n) \implies (\exists (z: \mathbb{Z}), \operatorname{sourceTerm}\left(F, n\right) = (\operatorname{PrimePowerShiftLogDerivative}.\operatorname{prime}\left(n\right): \mathbb{Q}) \cdot (z: \mathbb{Q}))))$$
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S1/Recurrence/Invariants/HannaPrimeIndexLogDivisibility.result` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Resolves.* `Problems/hanna-a381355` (proved) by `D5/S1/Recurrence/Invariants/HannaPrimeIndexLogDivisibility.result`.
+
+<!-- scribe-open-problem-resolution-v1 {"problem_slug":"hanna-a381355","declaration_gid":"D5/S1/Recurrence/Invariants/HannaPrimeIndexLogDivisibility.result","resolution_kind":"proved"} -->
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Acknowledgement.* Paul D. Hanna (2025). *OEIS A381355: prime-index divisibility of the logarithmic derivative of A381353*. URL: <https://oeis.org/A381355>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+Reduction modulo a prime makes all positive coefficients below that prime vanish in the corresponding power. Exact integral corrections therefore construct a source series. The coefficient change under a power gives uniqueness among rational source series. The formal derivative identity makes the relevant product coefficient zero over the integers; cancellation of the nonzero prime and reduction modulo that prime isolate the coefficient of the logarithmic derivative.
+

+import D5.S1.Recurrence.Parity.PrimePowerShiftLogDerivative
+import D5.S1.Recurrence.Invariants.UnitReversionSquareParity
+import D5.S1.Recurrence.LinearRows.LinearExponentDyadicSupport
+import D5.S1.Recurrence.Invariants.CubicFifteenSubstitutionParity
+import D5.S1.Recurrence.Residue.ContinuedFractionOddSquare
+
+/-! Hanna's source series is constructed over the integers and identified uniquely over the rationals. -/
+
+namespace D5.S1.Recurrence.Invariants.HannaPrimeIndexLogDivisibility
+open PowerSeries
+open D5.S1.Recurrence.Parity.PrimePowerShiftLogDerivative (prime)
+open D5.S1.Recurrence.Invariants.UnitReversionSquareParity (Agree agree_pow agree_mul)
+
+def IsSourceSeries (F : PowerSeries ℚ) : Prop :=
+  coeff 0 F = 1 ∧ coeff 1 F = 1 ∧
+    ∀ n : ℕ, 1 < n → coeff n (F ^ prime n) = 0
+
+noncomputable def sourceTerm (F : PowerSeries ℚ) (n : ℕ) : ℚ :=
+  coeff (n - 1) (derivative F * F⁻¹)
+
+def claim : Prop :=
+  (∃ F : PowerSeries ℚ, IsSourceSeries F) ∧
+    ∀ F : PowerSeries ℚ, IsSourceSeries F →
+      ∀ n : ℕ, 1 < n →
+        ∃ z : ℤ, sourceTerm F n = (prime n : ℚ) * (z : ℚ)
+
+private theorem low_prime_coeff (B : PowerSeries ℤ) {p j : ℕ}
+    (hp : Nat.Prime p) (hj : 1 ≤ j) (hjp : j < p) :
+    (p : ℤ) ∣ coeff j (B ^ p) := by
+  letI : Fact p.Prime := ⟨hp⟩
+  apply (ZMod.intCast_zmod_eq_zero_iff_dvd _ _).mp
+  change (Int.castRingHom (ZMod p)) (coeff j (B ^ p)) = 0
+  rw [← PowerSeries.coeff_map, map_pow,
+    D5.S1.Recurrence.Invariants.CubicFifteenSubstitutionParity.prime_power_subst,
+    coeff_subst_X_pow hp.ne_zero, if_neg (Nat.not_dvd_of_pos_of_lt (by omega) hjp)]
+
+private noncomputable def correction (n : ℕ) (B : PowerSeries ℤ) : ℤ :=
+  if n = 1 then 1 else -coeff n (B ^ prime n) / (prime n : ℤ)
+
+private noncomputable def advance (n : ℕ) (B : PowerSeries ℤ) : PowerSeries ℤ :=
+  B + C (correction n B) * X ^ n
+
+private theorem advance_agree (n : ℕ) (B : PowerSeries ℤ) : Agree n (advance n B) B := by
+  intro j hj
+  simp only [advance, map_add, coeff_C_mul_X_pow, if_neg (by omega : j ≠ n), add_zero]
+
+private theorem advance_zero {n : ℕ} (hn : 1 ≤ n) (B : PowerSeries ℤ)
+    (h0 : constantCoeff B = 1) : constantCoeff (advance n B) = 1 := by
+  simp [advance, h0, show n ≠ 0 by omega]
+
+private theorem correction_mul (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 < n) (B : PowerSeries ℤ) :
+    (prime n : ℤ) * correction n B = - coeff n (B ^ prime n) := by
+  have hp := D5.S1.Recurrence.Parity.PrimePowerShiftLogDerivative.prime_is_prime n
+  have hd : (prime n : ℤ) ∣ coeff n (B ^ prime n) :=
+    low_prime_coeff B hp (by omega) (by have := D5.S1.Recurrence.Parity.PrimePowerShiftLogDerivative.lt_prime n (by omega); omega)
+  rw [correction, if_neg (by omega)]
+  exact Int.mul_ediv_cancel' (dvd_neg.mpr hd)
+
+private theorem advance_equation {n : ℕ} (hn : 1 < n) (B : PowerSeries ℤ)
+    (h0 : constantCoeff B = 1) :
+    coeff n ((advance n B) ^ prime n) = 0 := by
+  have he := D5.S1.Recurrence.LinearRows.LinearExponentDyadicSupport.pow_change (advance_zero (by omega) B h0) h0 (advance_agree n B) (prime n)
+  have hadd : coeff n (advance n B) - coeff n B = correction n B := by
+    simp only [advance, map_add, coeff_C_mul_X_pow, ↓reduceIte, add_sub_cancel_left]
+  rw [hadd] at he
+  rw [correction_mul n hn B] at he
+  linear_combination he
+
+private noncomputable def approximation : ℕ → PowerSeries ℤ
+  | 0 => 1
+  | n + 1 => advance (n + 1) (approximation n)
+
+private theorem approximation_stable {s t : ℕ} (h : s ≤ t) :
+    Agree (s + 1) (approximation s) (approximation t) := by
+  induction t, h using Nat.le_induction with
+  | base => intro j hj; rfl
+  | succ t hst ih =>
+    intro j hj
+    exact (ih j hj).trans ((advance_agree (t + 1) (approximation t)) j (by omega)).symm
+
+private theorem approximation_zero (n : ℕ) : constantCoeff (approximation n) = 1 := by
+  simpa only [coeff_zero_eq_constantCoeff, approximation, map_one] using
+    (approximation_stable (s := 0) (t := n) (Nat.zero_le n) 0 (by omega)).symm
+
+private noncomputable def generatingSeries : PowerSeries ℤ :=
+  mk fun n => coeff n (approximation n)
+
+private theorem generating_agree (s : ℕ) : Agree (s + 1) generatingSeries (approximation s) := by
+  intro j hj
+  simpa only [generatingSeries, coeff_mk] using
+    approximation_stable (s := j) (t := s) (by omega) j (by omega)
+
+private theorem generating_equation_zero : constantCoeff generatingSeries = 1 ∧
+    ∀ n, 1 < n → coeff n (generatingSeries ^ prime n) = 0 := by
+  constructor
+  · simpa only [coeff_zero_eq_constantCoeff, approximation, map_one] using
+      generating_agree 0 0 (by omega)
+  · intro n hn
+    obtain ⟨k, rfl⟩ := Nat.exists_eq_succ_of_ne_zero (by omega : n ≠ 0)
+    rw [agree_pow (generating_agree (k + 1)) _ (k + 1) (by omega)]
+    exact advance_equation (by omega) _ (approximation_zero k)
+
+private noncomputable def logDerivative : PowerSeries ℤ :=
+  PowerSeries.derivative (R := ℤ) generatingSeries * invOfUnit generatingSeries 1
+
+private theorem log_mul : logDerivative * generatingSeries = PowerSeries.derivative (R := ℤ) generatingSeries := by
+  rw [logDerivative, mul_assoc, invOfUnit_mul _ 1 generating_equation_zero.1, mul_one]
+
+private theorem derivative_identity (n : ℕ) :
+    PowerSeries.derivative (R := ℤ) (generatingSeries ^ n) =
+      C (n : ℤ) * logDerivative * generatingSeries ^ n := by
+  cases n with
+  | zero => simp
+  | succ n =>
+    rw [derivative_pow, Nat.add_sub_cancel, pow_succ, ← log_mul]
+    have hc : (↑(n + 1) : PowerSeries ℤ) = C ((n + 1 : ℕ) : ℤ) := by simp
+    rw [hc]
+    ring
+
+private theorem source_divisibility (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 < n) :
+    (prime n : ℤ) ∣ coeff (n - 1) logDerivative := by
+  have hn1 : 1 ≤ n := by omega
+  have hp : (prime n : ℤ) ≠ 0 := by
+    exact_mod_cast (D5.S1.Recurrence.Parity.PrimePowerShiftLogDerivative.prime_is_prime n).ne_zero
+  have he := congrArg (coeff (n - 1)) (derivative_identity (prime n))
+  rw [coeff_derivative, Nat.sub_add_cancel hn1, mul_assoc, coeff_C_mul] at he
+  rw [show ((n - 1 : ℕ) : ℤ) + 1 = (n : ℤ) by omega] at he
+  rw [generating_equation_zero.2 n hn] at he
+  have he' : (prime n : ℤ) * coeff (n - 1) (logDerivative * generatingSeries ^ prime n) = 0 := by
+    simpa using he.symm
+  have hz : coeff (n - 1) (logDerivative * generatingSeries ^ prime n) = 0 := by
+    exact (mul_eq_zero.mp he').resolve_left hp
+  let f := Int.castRingHom (ZMod (prime n))
+  have ha : Agree n (PowerSeries.map f (generatingSeries ^ prime n)) 1 := by
+    intro j hj
+    by_cases hj0 : j = 0
+    · subst j
+      rw [PowerSeries.coeff_map]
+      simp [coeff_zero_eq_constantCoeff, generating_equation_zero.1]
+    · rw [PowerSeries.coeff_map, coeff_one, if_neg hj0]
+      exact (ZMod.intCast_zmod_eq_zero_iff_dvd _ _).mpr
+        (low_prime_coeff generatingSeries
+          (D5.S1.Recurrence.Parity.PrimePowerShiftLogDerivative.prime_is_prime n)
+          (by omega) (by have := D5.S1.Recurrence.Parity.PrimePowerShiftLogDerivative.lt_prime n hn1; omega))
+  have heq := agree_mul (f := PowerSeries.map f logDerivative)
+    (g := PowerSeries.map f logDerivative) (fun _ _ => rfl) ha (n - 1) (by omega)
+  rw [← map_mul, PowerSeries.coeff_map, hz, map_zero, mul_one] at heq
+  exact (ZMod.intCast_zmod_eq_zero_iff_dvd _ _).mp (by
+    simpa [f, PowerSeries.coeff_map] using heq.symm)
+
+private noncomputable def castSeries : PowerSeries ℚ :=
+  PowerSeries.map (Int.castRingHom ℚ) generatingSeries
+
+private theorem castSeries_source : IsSourceSeries castSeries := by
+  refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_⟩
+  · simpa [castSeries, coeff_zero_eq_constantCoeff] using
+      congrArg (Int.castRingHom ℚ) generating_equation_zero.1
+  · have hgen : coeff 1 generatingSeries = 1 := by
+      calc
+        coeff 1 generatingSeries = coeff 1 (approximation 1) := generating_agree 1 1 (by omega)
+        _ = 1 := by simp [approximation, advance, correction]
+    simpa [castSeries] using congrArg (Int.castRingHom ℚ) hgen
+  · intro n hn
+    change coeff n ((PowerSeries.map (Int.castRingHom ℚ) generatingSeries) ^ prime n) = 0
+    rw [← map_pow, PowerSeries.coeff_map]
+    exact congrArg (Int.castRingHom ℚ) (generating_equation_zero.2 n hn)
+
+private theorem generating_uniqueQ (B : PowerSeries ℚ) (h0 : constantCoeff B = 1)
+    (h1 : coeff 1 B = 1)
+    (hB : ∀ n, 1 < n → coeff n (B ^ prime n) = 0) : B = castSeries := by
+  ext n
+  induction n using Nat.strong_induction_on with
+  | h n ih =>
+    by_cases hn0 : n = 0
+    · subst n
+      simpa only [coeff_zero_eq_constantCoeff, castSeries_source.1] using h0
+    by_cases hn1 : n = 1
+    · subst n
+      simpa only [castSeries_source.2.1] using h1
+    have hag : Agree n B castSeries := by
+      intro j hj
+      exact ih j (by omega)
+    have hp : (prime n : ℚ) ≠ 0 := by
+      exact_mod_cast (D5.S1.Recurrence.Parity.PrimePowerShiftLogDerivative.prime_is_prime n).ne_zero
+    have h0' : constantCoeff castSeries = 1 := by simpa [coeff_zero_eq_constantCoeff] using castSeries_source.1
+    have he := D5.S1.Recurrence.LinearRows.LinearExponentDyadicSupport.pow_change h0 h0' hag (prime n)
+    rw [hB n (by omega), castSeries_source.2.2 n (by omega), sub_self] at he
+    exact sub_eq_zero.mp ((mul_eq_zero.mp he.symm).resolve_left hp)
+
+private theorem map_invOfUnit :
+    PowerSeries.map (Int.castRingHom ℚ) (invOfUnit generatingSeries 1) =
+      (PowerSeries.map (Int.castRingHom ℚ) generatingSeries)⁻¹ := by
+  rw [D5.S1.Recurrence.Residue.ContinuedFractionOddSquare.map_inverse
+    (Int.castRingHom ℚ) generatingSeries generating_equation_zero.1]
+  apply invOfUnit_eq'
+  simpa only [castSeries, coeff_zero_eq_constantCoeff, Units.val_one] using castSeries_source.1
+
+private theorem sourceTerm_cast (n : ℕ) :
+    sourceTerm castSeries n =
+      (Int.castRingHom ℚ) (coeff (n - 1) logDerivative) := by
+  rw [sourceTerm, castSeries,
+    ← D5.S1.Recurrence.LinearRows.LinearExponentDyadicSupport.derivative_map,
+    ← map_invOfUnit, ← map_mul]
+  rfl
+
+theorem result : claim := by
+  constructor
+  · exact ⟨castSeries, castSeries_source⟩
+  · intro F hF n hn
+    have h0F : constantCoeff F = 1 := by simpa [coeff_zero_eq_constantCoeff] using hF.1
+    have huniq := generating_uniqueQ F h0F hF.2.1 hF.2.2
+    obtain ⟨z, hz⟩ := source_divisibility n hn
+    refine ⟨z, ?_⟩
+    rw [huniq, sourceTerm_cast]
+    simpa using congrArg (Int.castRingHom ℚ) hz

+# Hanna's A381355 prime-index divisibility
+
+## Problem
+
+Paul D. Hanna's [OEIS A381355](https://oeis.org/A381355), revision 13,
+COMMENTS (unpaginated), states:
+
+> Conjecture: a(n) is divisible by prime(n) for n > 1.
+
+Its NAME defines $a_n=[x^{n-1}]F'(x)/F(x)$, where the source
+[OEIS A381353](https://oeis.org/A381353), revision 19, satisfies
+$[x^n]F(x)^{p_n}=0$ for every $n>1$. Its PROGRAM initializes
+`my(A=[1,1])`, fixing $[x^0]F=[x^1]F=1$. Here $p_n$ is the one-based
+prime schedule, with $p_1=2$. Source and literature evidence is recorded in
+[preregistration #23982](https://github.com/the-omega-institute/trureturing/issues/23982)
+and the [Library note](../Library/RecurrenceComposition/hanna2025a381355.md).
+
+### Statement echo
+
+| Source clause | Lean counterpart | Fidelity |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Source coefficients zero and one are one | `IsSourceSeries` first two conjuncts | Literal initialization. |
+| Zero prime-power diagonal for every $n>1$ | `IsSourceSeries` third conjunct | Literal coefficient equation. |
+| One-based primes | Reused `PrimePowerShiftLogDerivative.prime` | $p_1=2$; no new prime function. |
+| $a_n=[x^{n-1}]F'/F$ | `sourceTerm` | Formal derivative times formal inverse, with the coefficient shift. |
+| Divisible by $p_n$ for every $n>1$ | `claim` universal conjunct | An integer witness in the rationals, rather than field divisibility. |
+| Implicit source exists | `claim` existential conjunct | Additional conclusion prevents vacuity. |
+| Any rational source satisfying the equations | Universal source binder in `claim` | No integrality hypothesis or chosen-source restriction. |
+
+No clause is dropped. Natural subtraction occurs only at $n>1$ in the
+assertion. Inversion is applied to series of constant coefficient one.
+There is no asserted divisibility at $n=0$ or $n=1$.
+
+## Motivation
+
+The conjecture relates an implicit source to the logarithmic derivative
+of that same source. Integral construction and rational uniqueness identify
+this common realization; independent finite coefficient lists do not do so.
+
+## Gap
+
+The named conjecture is proved by
+`D5.S1.Recurrence.Invariants.HannaPrimeIndexLogDivisibility.result`.
+The four-slot escape audit for this public theorem is unfinished:
+[#24211](https://github.com/the-omega-institute/trureturing/issues/24211).
+No Reg mirror or validated registration is claimed. The missing evidence is
+a source-bound dependent-family realization of the existential/universal
+conjunction with compiled reconstruction, bridge, variation, sensitivity
+and actual dependence proofs.
+
+## Route
+
+All auxiliary names below belong to
+`D5.S1.Recurrence.Invariants.HannaPrimeIndexLogDivisibility` and are private.
+At stage $n$, `correction` changes only coefficient $n$ by an integer.
+`low_prime_coeff` applies the imported Frobenius owner
+`CubicFifteenSubstitutionParity.prime_power_subst` to show divisibility
+of every positive coefficient below the prime. The imported
+`LinearExponentDyadicSupport.pow_change` supplies the coefficient-change
+identity used by `advance_equation` and `generating_uniqueQ`.
+`approximation_stable` and `generating_agree` form the compatible infinite
+integral source, and `generating_equation_zero` verifies its zero diagonal.
+`castSeries_source` and `generating_uniqueQ` identify every rational source
+with its integer-coefficient realization. `source_divisibility` combines
+formal differentiation, integer cancellation and reduction modulo the
+indexed prime. `sourceTerm_cast` transports that divisibility to the
+source's rational coefficient convention, and `result` supplies existence
+and universal divisibility together.
+
+## Falsifier
+
+A rational source satisfying the stated initial and diagonal equations,
+and an index $n>1$ whose logarithmic-derivative coefficient is outside
+$p_n\mathbb Z$, would contradict `result`. No extra existence or
+integrality hypothesis is assumed by that theorem. The experiment's
+$n=1$ value is $a_1=1$, which is not divisible by $p_1=2$; this boundary
+is outside the source assertion.
+

+in Route. The Blueprint displays the expanded claim. The module is

+Finite computations are evidence about examples and source fidelity,

+### What the settlement shows
+
+The decisive mechanism is an integral coefficient correction followed by
+cancellation before reduction modulo a prime. Frobenius makes the required
+correction integral because $0<n<p_n$. Stabilization gives a genuine infinite
+series, and rational coefficient induction gives uniqueness. The coefficient
+of degree $n-1$ in the derivative identity vanishes over the integers; after
+cancelling the nonzero prime, all lower positive coefficients in the prime
+power vanish modulo that prime, leaving the required logarithmic-derivative
+coefficient. These claims are kernel-checked by the private declarations
+named in Route and the public `result`.
+
+The resulting conclusion settles the A381355 COMMENTS conjecture and the
+matching A381353 COMMENTS assertion under the source initialization.
+The wider schedule/slope family is open as a formal target. There is no
+asymptotic or sign-pattern conclusion, and no consequence for the distinct
+A393866/A393867 source equation. No inspected source identifies an additional
+result that depends on the conjecture.
